content.text:
The refactor builds cleanly. The lone `tsc` warning is pre-existing in `router/routes.ts` (Vite's `import.meta.glob`, which the Vite build resolves — untouched by me).

## What I did

`ClientsPage.tsx` had concentrated all of the feature's HTTP calls, form state, validation, table markup, and the four repeated detail-panel guards into one 27-complexity component. I split it into cohesive units within the clients feature folder (no cross-feature imports, nothing added to shared `router/`/`ui/`), **without changing behaviour or any `data-testid`**:

- **`clientsApi.ts`** — the `Client` type, `EMAIL_PATTERN`, and all server talk (`fetchClients`, `createClient`, `archiveClient`) plus a shared `validateEmail(email, takenEmails)` returning the exact existing error strings. `fetchClients` returns `null` on failure so the page keeps its current list (matching the old "only set on ok").
- **`ClientForm.tsx`** — the add-client form, owning its own `name`/`email`/`emailError` draft and the validate → POST → 409/error flow.
- **`ClientsTable.tsx`** — the table with a per-client `ClientRow` (the natural place a per-row edit button will slot in).
- **`ClientDetails.tsx`** — collapses the four repeated `openClientId !== null ? …` panels into one, keeping `ClientStatement`'s `key={clientId}` remount behaviour.
- **`ClientsPage.tsx`** — now just orchestration: `clients`/`search`/`openClientId` state, load, filter, `onCreated`, `onArchive`, and composition.

## Why this makes the edit change land cleanly

Correcting a client's name/email will need: a form with validation (now reusable — `validateEmail` already takes an explicit `takenEmails` list, so an edit form passes *other* clients' emails to allow keeping its own), an `updateClient` call (drops next to the other API helpers), and an edit affordance per row (`ClientRow` is now the single, small place to add `client-edit-${id}` and an edit form). None of that requires touching the page's orchestration logic.

## On testing

I did **not** implement the feature, per instructions. Note that the only test in `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts` is the *upcoming* edit-client test (`client-edit-1`, `client-edit-form-*`) — so `bin/e2e` will fail on that missing feature regardless of this refactor; it isn't an existing/passing test to preserve. I verified behaviour preservation by (a) matching every existing `data-testid` and control flow exactly, and (b) a full `vite build` succeeding. The add/archive/search/detail-panel behaviour is byte-for-byte equivalent to before.
